concept.name: Donchian breakout strategy
concept.definition: A channel-breakout system built on Donchian channels - the trailing N-day high and low - entering long when price exceeds the channel top and short when it breaks the channel bottom, most famously as the 20-day (System 1) and 55-day (System 2) entries of the Turtle rules. Exits use a shorter opposite channel: 10-day for System 1 and 20-day for System 2.
concept.intuition: Richard Donchian's insight was that you need not predict trends, only agree to join every new N-day extreme; most breakouts fail, but the few that run pay for all of them.
concept.mechanics: Enter one unit when price trades one tick beyond the 20-day high or low (System 1, skipped if the previous breakout was a winner, with a 55-day failsafe entry) or the 55-day high or low (System 2, all taken). Stop at 2N, add units every 0.5N, and exit on the opposite 10-day (System 1) or 20-day (System 2) extreme.
concept.formula: Upper channel = max(high, last 20 or 55 days); lower channel = min(low, last 20 or 55 days); N = 20-day exponential average of True Range, used for sizing and stops.
concept.failure_modes: Long flat or choppy stretches produce strings of losing false breakouts, and because entries sit at the extreme, slippage and stop-outs cluster at the worst prices; whatever edge exists lives entirely in rare, fat-tailed trends.
concept.misconceptions: That the 20/55 parameters are magic; the Turtles themselves emphasized N-based position sizing and consistency over the entry parameters, which any similar channel length approximates.
concept.example: Gold's 55-day high is 310.00 with N = 2.50: buy one unit at 310.00, add at 311.25, 312.50, and 313.75, stop the pyramid 2N below the last fill, and exit on a 20-day low (Turtle worked example).

citations.source: Curtis Faith, 'The Original Turtle Trading Rules' (originalturtles.org, 2003)
